title.narrative: Improving sustainability of water supply services through systems strengthening, in Awdal Region, Somaliland.

description.narrative: Direct target groups:(1) Micro level:2,100 households (12,600 individuals) from the 9 targeted communities benefitting from sustainable water supply services;9 Water Management Committees (WMCs) with a total of 63 members trained on water point operation, maintenance and tariff collection;18 water point operators/technicians who will be trained and working closely with the WMCs to manage the water sources.(2)Meso level: 3 members of government authorities in the target area participating in the long-term capacity development support.;18 members of LNGOs/INGOs in the target area that benefit from capacity-building support and/or orientation on systems strengthening approaches and advocating for change in key areas.(3)Macro level :6 members of government authorities at the national and regional levels that benefit from capacity-building support and greater connectivity between humanitarian and developmental actors and actions; 30 members of LNGOs/INGOs at the national and regional levels that benefit from direct capacity-building support, strengthened multi-stakeholder coordination and dialogue platforms, and/or holding governmental actors accountable and advocating on key issues.;23 TAAKULO staff benefitting from programmatic and non programmatic capacity building initiatives.

The overall objective (impact) of the project: Sustainable water supply systems and governance in the Awdal Region are enabled.Outcome: In the 9 target communities, the population benefits from functional water supply services and sustainable management of water resources.

To mitigate against persistent challenges in the water supply sectors, WHH and TAAKULO jointly propose to pilot a systems approach to water supply that integrates the relevant actors (key stakeholders from community, regional and national level service authorities) and factors (financial, institutional, environmental, political etc.) toward sustainable water supply services.
